analysis:
The PR adds four build-time Python scripts and no runtime provider code: scripts/check-date-comparisons.py (regex-based source lint for Date >=/<=), scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py (nm/otool binary check for the weak Foundation Date.>=/<= imports), and their unit tests. None of them touch the coordinator WebSocket, keys, attestation, the prefix cache, the fan helper, the add-on hold socket, or the sandbox installer. I found no changed security behavior against TB-002/003/007/009/010/011/012/013, or A-001..A-019, T-041 included.

I checked the binary checker for command injection. subprocess.run receives list arguments with no shell, so a binary path cannot inject commands. The tool names nm, otool and xcrun come from PATH, which is a standard CI assumption and not a new boundary. The regex patterns are linear and bounded. A path argument is only passed to nm and otool. A missing or unreadable binary fails closed (exit 1, via CalledProcessError or the explicit is_file check).

The symbol-denylist approach covers only the two Date operator mangled names, so other back-deployed symbols would not be flagged. That is a coverage limit of a build-hygiene check, not a security regression. The source lint documents that it can miss comparisons and names the binary check as the complete guard. The availability benefit is that it prevents a provider crash loop on affected macOS builds (loosely related to T-057 availability). How CI invokes check-provider-weak-imports.py on release artifacts is not in the supplied evidence (no workflow file in this batch), so enforcement is unverified. The test file runs the lint against shipped sources, which is read-only. No findings.
